title: No Content-Security-Policy: sole XSS defense is React escaping, and any injection immediately exfiltrates the 24h admin JWT in localStorage
evidence: main.go:99-101 sets only three headers: `h.Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")` / `h.Set("X-Frame-Options", "DENY")` / `h.Set("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin")` — no Content-Security-Policy. frontend/index.html (lines 1-12) is a bare SPA shell with no CSP meta either: `<title>AI 网关管理平台</title>` is the only head content besides charset/viewport. Meanwhile the admin JWT is persisted readable to any script: frontend/src/store/auth.ts:28 `storage: createJSONStorage(() => localStorage),`, with 24h validity (backend/internal/auth/jwt.go:21 `ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour)),`) and no server-side revocation (backend/internal/admin/auth.go:152-153 logout only does `s.recordOp(c, "login", "auth", "logout", nil, nil)`).
impact: The console deliberately renders attacker-influenced gateway content (call input/output text, model aliases, api_key_label, block_reason, error_msg, WS frames). I audited every sink: grep for dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|document.write|eval(|new Function across frontend/src returns ZERO matches; JsonView.tsx:46 renders `{text}` (JSON.parse/stringify round-trip) as a React text child; Calls.tsx:348/362 render `{detail.input_text || t('calls.none')}` as escaped children; LiveAuditStream.tsx:87-97 render WS frame fields via Typography.Text children (escaped); dicts.ts:176 falls back to the raw value but is rendered as React text; Help.tsx uses `<Trans>` with a fixed component whitelist; i18n/index.ts:63 `escapeValue: false` is safe only because all t() output lands in React children; AccountSecurity.tsx:165 is a fixed `data:image/png;base64,` prefix so no scheme swap. So no XSS exists TODAY. The gap: any single future escaping bypass (new feature, antd upgrade, a `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` import) converts directly into admin account takeover (localStorage JWT, not HttpOnly) with no script-src to block exfiltration, and no frame-ancestors beyond XFO (XFO ignored by some non-browser embed contexts and by any future same-origin HTML injection serving).
mitigations_checked: Full-sink grep (no HTML sinks anywhere in frontend/src *.ts/*.tsx); React auto-escaping in Calls.tsx detail drawer, JsonView.tsx, LiveAuditStream.tsx, antd message.error(body.message) at client.ts:80 (React children, escaped); X-Frame-Options DENY and nosniff present; only href/src sink is AccountSecurity.tsx:165 data:image/png QR from authenticated API.
recommendation: Serve `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' ws: wss:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'` from the same header middleware in main.go:97-103 (style-src unsafe-inline is required by antd v5's cssinjs; tighten to nonce later if pursued). Also migrate the admin JWT out of localStorage to an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie (with CSRF protection) or at least add a short TTL + server-side revocation so a future injection is not a durable ATO.

title: Admin JWT passed as `?token=` query string on the audit WebSocket — leaks into reverse-proxy/LB access logs; token is 24h valid and non-revocable, so any log reader gets admin takeover
evidence: frontend/src/hooks/useAuditStream.ts:65: `const url = `${proto}//${window.location.host}/api/admin/v1/audit/ws?token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`;` — consumed by backend/internal/admin/auditws.go:31: `claims, err := auth.Parse(s.secret, c.Query("token"))` on a route that deliberately skips the Bearer-header middleware (backend/internal/admin/routes.go:118 `api.GET("/audit/ws", s.auditWS)`). README.md:306 documents the intended production topology: `> Put a front LB (Nginx / HAProxy / cloud LB) round-robining gateway-a:8080 / gateway-b:8080` — the WS handshake request line `GET /api/admin/v1/audit/ws?token=<JWT> HTTP/1.1` lands verbatim in every intermediary that logs full request URIs (nginx's default combined format logs `$request`). jwt.go:21 gives the token a 24h expiry, and auth.go:152-153 `logout` is log-only with no revocation list, so a leaked token stays valid until it expires.
impact: Anyone who can read a proxy/LB/web-server access log, a log-aggregation pipeline (ELK/SIEM), or a support bundle obtains a fully-privileged admin JWT valid up to 24h that logout cannot kill — full admin-console takeover. If the deployment is plain HTTP (see frontend-3), a network on-path attacker sees the handshake URL with no log access required, which escalates this to direct account takeover on the same LAN. Note the URL also persists in the browser's own process state (WebSocket object, crash dumps, browser-sync/extension tools), and the query param is the ONLY place the JWT is transmitted this way — all other admin routes use the Authorization header (middleware.go:16), confirming this is an avoidable special case.
mitigations_checked: App's own access log does NOT capture the query: main.go:109 `path := c.Request.URL.Path` and main.go:116-117 log only `path` — so the in-app log is clean; exposure is confined to front proxies/OS-level TCP visibility. Auth is rejected before upgrade with 401 (auditws.go:32-35), so no half-open session. No cookies are involved, so a cross-site page cannot ride the connection without knowing the token (no classic CSWSH). encodeURIComponent is applied. Origin header is not validated in auditws.go — noted as a hardening gap, though token-required auth means it is not independently exploitable.
recommendation: Replace the long-lived JWT in the query with a single-use, short-TTL (seconds) WS ticket: authenticated `POST /audit/ws-ticket` returns a random one-time nonce stored server-side (or an HMAC with exp+scope); the WS URL carries only the nonce, which is redeemed once at handshake and grants read-only stream scope. Additionally validate `Origin` against the configured host in auditws.go, and if the query token is retained, document `log_format` scrubbing for nginx (`$uri` instead of `$request`).

title: TLS is nowhere implemented or deployed: server is HTTP-only on all interfaces, in-app help and all deployment docs instruct callers to send sk- keys and admin logins over `http://<server-IP>:8080` — violating the project's own PRD NFR-008 ("Over HTTPS only")
evidence: main.go:126 `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}` with main.go:134 `err := srv.ListenAndServe()` — plaintext, bound to all interfaces; grep for `ListenAndServeTLS|tls.Config|autocert` across backend/**/*.go returns zero matches, so the product has no TLS capability at all. The product's own help actively normalizes cleartext: frontend/src/i18n/locales/en-US/pages/help.ts:38 `...deploy to a public/internal server; callers use <c2>http://<server-IP-or-domain>:8080/v1/...</c2>...` (zh-CN identical at line 38; help.ts:7 likewise gives `http://<your-host>:<port>/v1` as THE public address). TLS exists only as one bullet: help.ts:55 `'TLS / reverse proxy': 'Built-in serves HTTP; in production front it with Nginx to terminate TLS...'` — yet deploy/ contains no reverse-proxy or TLS example (grep for `https|tls|nginx|cert` across deploy/*.sh: the only hits are `sslmode=disable` in env.sh:4 and verify_schema.sh:35, i.e. TLS explicitly disabled). Production recipes stop at HTTP: quickstart.en.md:137 `PORT=8080 DB_TYPE=sqlite DB_DSN=/var/lib/llm-router-guard/gateway.db \` and README.md:156 `- "8080:8080"`. Meanwhile prd.en.md:482 states the requirement: `| NFR-008 | Security | API Key transmission | Over HTTPS only |`.
impact: The default and only documented deployment path puts (a) gateway API keys `sk-<32hex>` in the Authorization/x-api-key header, (b) admin login POST credentials, (c) the entire 24h JWT (including the query-string JWT of frontend-2), and (d) all proxied prompt/completion traffic, in cleartext on a socket bound to 0.0.0.0. Any same-LAN/passive-tap attacker captures reusable admin and gateway credentials and all routed LLM payloads. This is a repo-wide posture gap, not just operator error: the guidance the software itself emits leads with http:// URLs and the PRD's own hard requirement is unmet with no worked example to close it.
mitigations_checked: Referrer-Policy/nosniff/XFO present (main.go:99-101) but do not protect transit; same-origin SPA + no CORS limits browser-based reads, not network sniffing; TRUSTED_PROXIES defaults empty so IP-spoofing is separate (known). Gateway keys are SHA-256 hashed at rest (auditws/help notes) — irrelevant to wire exposure. The in-app TLS bullet exists but has no matching config example anywhere in repo.
recommendation: Ship a worked TLS front in deploy/ (an `nginx.conf` example terminating TLS with HSTS, proxying to 127.0.0.1:8080, using `$uri` logging per frontend-2, and the matching TRUSTED_PROXIES setting), and make quickstart §8/README compose examples bind `127.0.0.1:8080:8080` behind it; optionally add `TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE` env vars calling `ListenAndServeTLS` in main.go. Update help.addrBody/help.deployBody to present `https://` as the canonical public address and label `http://` as local-only.

title: Commit-ready admin credentials in deploy scripts: known JWT_SECRET/MASTER_KEY/ADMIN_PASSWORD (and DB root password with TLS disabled) — reusable HS256 secret means anyone can forge admin tokens
evidence: deploy/run_server.sh:13-14 `JWT_SECRET="e2e-jwt-secret-2026" MASTER_KEY="e2e-master-key-2026" \` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD="E2eAdmin#2026" GIN_MODE=release \` — this is the only server-launch script in deploy/ (invoked by do_all.sh), and it runs with `GIN_MODE=release`. deploy/env.sh:3-6 `export DB_MYSQL_DSN='root:comeback@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/gateway_mysql?...'`, `export DB_PG_DSN='host=127.0.0.1 port=5432 user=postgres password=comeback dbname=gateway_pg sslmode=disable ...'`, `export MYSQL_PWD=comeback`, `export PGPASSWORD=comeback`; deploy/verify_schema.sh:35 repeats the postgres DSN.
impact: The scripts are E2E fixtures, but they are public, functional, and the canonical 'how to start the server' example in the repo: an HS256 secret committed to the source tree lets anyone forge a valid admin JWT (jwt.go:26 `SignedString([]byte(secret))`, no kid/jti pinning) against any deployment that reused these values — full admin takeover without a password. A committed MASTER_KEY additionally means AES-GCM-encrypted vendor keys are decryptable for such deployments. The DB password (`root:comeback`) and `sslmode=disable` round out a credential set likely to leak into real environments (this exact pattern — copy the deploy script, change the port — is how self-hosted app defaults end up on the public internet).
mitigations_checked: File headers label them as E2E-only ('Environment for gateway E2E tests'); values are non-default-vs-code constants, so an operator who runs env.sh unmodified in production also gets main.go's warnInsecureDefaults only for the unset-var case, not for these set-but-known values. No git-secrets/pre-commit scanning found.
recommendation: Generate these per-run in the scripts (`JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)`) or source from an untracked `deploy/.env.test` listed in .gitignore with a committed `.env.test.example`; add a loud header comment and refuse to run if `E2E_OK=1` is not set. Purge the literals from git history if the repo is published.
